Release metadata (from GitHub Releases page)
- Repository: microsoft/playwright
- Releases page: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/releases
- Newest non‑preview release: v1.62.1
- Tag: v1.62.1
- Publication date (as shown on Releases page): 30 Jul 2026

Three concrete changes from the v1.62.1 release notes (non‑preview)
1) TypeScript configuration resolution bug fix (#41989)
   - Change: Fixed how Playwright resolves a tsconfig.json when the tsconfig uses an "extends" field that is a bare package specifier. Previously these extended configs were not correctly located/resolved, causing TypeScript project configuration issues.
   - Evidence: v1.62.1 release notes list a bug fix for issue #41989 that specifically mentions handling of tsconfig "extends" bare specifier resolution.

2) Directory‑form tsconfig project references bug fix (#41998)
   - Change: Fixed support for using directory‑form project references in TypeScript (where a referenced project is specified by a directory rather than a specific tsconfig file). Earlier, such directory references could fail or not be interpreted correctly by Playwright’s tooling.
   - Evidence: v1.62.1 release notes include a bug fix for #41998 describing that directory‑form tsconfig project references now work correctly.

3) Accessibility snapshot button‑name bug fix (#41985)
   - Change: Fixed ariaSnapshot / toMatchAriaSnapshot behavior where a button’s accessible name could be dropped from the snapshot when the button text was wrapped in spans and an SVG with aria-hidden="true" was present. After the fix, the accessibility snapshot correctly preserves the button’s accessible name in these cases.
   - Evidence: v1.62.1 release notes list a bug fix for #41985 describing that accessibility snapshots had been dropping button names when text was nested inside spans alongside an aria-hidden SVG, and that this behavior is now corrected.

Official documentation verification for the accessibility snapshot behavior
Goal: Verify, using Playwright’s official ARIA snapshot documentation, that button entries in accessibility snapshots include their accessible names. This directly confirms the behavior that the bug fix #41985 intends to preserve.

Documentation consulted
- URL: https://playwright.dev/docs/aria-snapshots
- Page title: "Snapshot testing | Playwright"

Relevant documentation excerpts and interpretation
1) Definition of ARIA snapshot node format (from the "Aria snapshots" section)
   - The documentation explains how each accessible element is represented:
     - It states that each element is represented with the YAML pattern:
       - `- role "name" [attribute=value]`
     - It further clarifies that:
       - `role`: is the ARIA or HTML role (e.g. heading, list, listitem, button).
       - The quoted string after the role is the accessible name of the element.
   - Interpretation:
     - For a button, this pattern becomes something like `- button "Submit"` where "Submit" is the button’s accessible name. This shows that, by design, button entries in the accessibility snapshot format include their accessible names when those names are present.

2) Concrete example explicitly showing a button with accessible name
   - In the "Attributes and states" subsection, under the heading "Button with pressed attribute", the documentation shows the following HTML and snapshot:
     - HTML example:
       - `<button aria-pressed="true">Toggle</button>`
     - Corresponding ARIA snapshot example:
       - `- button "Toggle" [pressed=true]`
   - Interpretation:
     - The snapshot node clearly uses the role `button`, followed by the quoted accessible name "Toggle" and the attribute [pressed=true].
     - This explicitly demonstrates that a button’s accessible name ("Toggle") is part of its snapshot entry.

3) Partial matching example reinforcing that buttons normally have a name
   - In the "Partial matching" section, the documentation presents:
     - HTML example:
       - `<button>Submit</button>`
     - Snapshot example used for partial matching:
       - `- button`
   - The associated explanation notes that in this partial match, the button role is matched but the accessible name ("Submit") is not specified, so the test passes regardless of label.
   - Interpretation:
     - The text explicitly refers to the accessible name of the button as "Submit", implying that, in the full (non‑partial) snapshot, the node would be `- button "Submit"` (i.e., including its accessible name). The partial snapshot intentionally omits the name for flexibility, but the documentation assumes the underlying snapshot has the name.

How this documentation verifies the bug fix #41985
- The bug fix description (from the release notes) states that accessibility snapshots previously dropped a button’s name when the text content was nested inside spans along with an aria-hidden SVG. The intended correct behavior is that the accessibility snapshot must still include the button’s accessible name even with such markup.
- The ARIA snapshot documentation provides the normative expected behavior:
  1) The general node format requires that each accessible element may include an accessible name after the role: `- role "name" [attribute=value]`.
  2) The "Button with pressed attribute" example concretely shows a button represented as `- button "Toggle" [pressed=true]`, where "Toggle" is the accessible name.
  3) The "Partial matching" button example explicitly speaks about the button’s accessible name ("Submit") and shows that omitting the name is an intentional testing relaxation, not a normal snapshot omission.
- Therefore, according to the official documentation, button entries in aria snapshots are supposed to include their accessible names in standard snapshots. The bug fix in #41985 ensures that this documented behavior is honored even when the DOM structure uses nested spans and aria-hidden SVGs. In other words, the fix restores conformance with the ARIA snapshot specification demonstrated by the examples on https://playwright.dev/docs/aria-snapshots.

Summary
- Newest non‑preview Microsoft Playwright release on GitHub Releases: v1.62.1, tag v1.62.1, published 30 Jul 2026.
- Three concrete changes confirmed from the v1.62.1 release notes:
  1) Correct handling of tsconfig "extends" bare specifiers (#41989).
  2) Support for directory‑form TypeScript project references in tsconfig (#41998).
  3) Fix for accessibility snapshots dropping button accessible names when text is inside spans with an aria-hidden SVG (#41985).
- Official Playwright documentation on ARIA snapshots confirms that button entries in snapshots include their accessible names (e.g., `- button "Toggle" [pressed=true]`), and describes the general `- role "name" [...]` pattern. This documented behavior matches what the accessibility snapshot bug fix in #41985 restores, thereby directly verifying the intended, correct behavior of aria snapshots for buttons with accessible names.
